item.title: Rolfes reveals why Hofmann was chosen over Boniface for Leverkusen's Europa League squad
item.description: Rolfes reveals why Hofmann was chosen over Boniface for Leverkusen's Europa League squad Following Martin Terrier's injury, Bayer Leverkusen have decided to include Jonas Hofmann in their Europa League squad as the Frenchman's replacement. This means Victor Boniface will remain out of the squad for Thursday's Europa League clash against OFI, with Bayer Leverkusen managing director for sport Simon Rolfes explaining the decision ahead of the team's departure for Crete. “Jonas is a very versatile player who can play in different positions. I think it's important to have different types of players available for different situations. If we could have, we would have liked to take both, but we decided on Jonas, and he will be with us tomorrow,” Rolfes said, according to Kölner Stadt-Anzeiger. Boniface played a key role in Leverkusen's success under Xabi Alonso, helping Die Werkself secure the domestic double. However, recurring injuries, particularly knee problems, have hampered his progress since then. So far this season, the Nigerian forward has been limited to just five minutes of action this season, but Rolfes believes his opportunity will come. “This doesn't change Boni's situation. He needs to stay fit, keep working hard and continue improving, and then his opportunity will come. I'm not worried. His most difficult situation came in early summer, and he has worked his way out of it. Since then, he has been in a much better place, mentally as well, and can once again see many more opportunities ahead of him,” the Leverkusen chief said. “In terms of intensity, pressing and working against the ball were never his main strengths, even when he was playing and scoring goals. He has other qualities. We want to get his fitness level as high as possible so that he can showcase his undoubted abilities even more effectively.”

item.title: RFEF confirms four-match suspension for Real Betis midfielder after clash with Lamine Yamal
item.description: RFEF confirms four-match suspension for Real Betis midfielder after clash with Lamine Yamal Real Betis midfielder Facundo Bernal has been handed a four-match suspension following his confrontation with Barcelona forward Lamine Yamal, with the RFEF Disciplinary Committee ruling that the incident constituted an assault under Spanish football’s disciplinary regulations. As reported by Mundo Deportivo , the punishment follows Bernal’s red card during Betis’ meeting with Barcelona last Saturday. The midfielder was dismissed after an altercation with Yamal, who intervened when tensions escalated around teammate Fermin Lopez. RFEF explains why Bernal received a four-match suspension The disciplinary committee based its decision on the referee’s account of the incident and Article 103 of the Disciplinary Code, which covers assaults committed without causing injury. Ricardo de Burgos Bengoechea’s report described the sequence that led to Bernal’s dismissal in the 54th minute, making clear that the confrontation involved physical contact while the ball was out of play. “In the 54th minute, player (6) FACUNDO BERNAL CRUZ was sent off for the following reason: during a confrontation, this player grabbed an opponent by the neck and headbutted him twice in quick succession in the face, whilst the ball was not in play. “The opposing player did not require medical attention and was able to continue the match,” the referee’s report stated Notably, Article 103 provides for a suspension of four to twelve matches when a player assaults another person without causing injury, with the fact that play has stopped serving as a determining factor in establishing intent. Bernal has received the minimum four-match punishment under that provision. How the confrontation with Lamine Yamal unfolded The incident began shortly after half-time, when Betis goalkeeper Alvaro Valles attempted to help Fermin Lopez up while the Barcelona midfielder was on the ground. Yamal stepped in to support his teammate, bringing him into a confrontation with Bernal. Facundo Bernal has been given a four-match ban. (Photo by Fran Santiago/Getty Images) The Betis midfielder first grabbed Yamal before the exchange escalated into a clash of heads. item.title: Opponent watch: Barcelona midfielder out of Real Madrid clash through injury
item.description: Opponent watch: Barcelona midfielder out of Real Madrid clash through injury Ahead of the weekend blockbuster encounter at the Spotify Camp Nou against Real Madrid, FC Barcelona have suffered a major injury setback. According to Carlos Monfort of SPORT , the Blaugrana have lost attacking midfielder Dani Olmo to an adductor tear with the Spanish international now set to miss the first El Clasico of the 2026/27 season. Olmo injured Olmo suffered the injury during Barcelona’s 4-2 loss to Paris Saint-Germain in the UEFA Champions League on Tuesday night. The 2026 FIFA World Cup winner was part of the starting XI for Barça at Parc des Princes, but lasted only 27 minutes as he suffered a muscle injury following a collision with Vitinha. Olmo is injured. (Photo by Justin Setterfield/Getty Images) After being assessed by the medical staff, he was withdrawn by manager Hansi Flick, with Fermin Lopez replacing him on the field. Now, following tests conducted earlier today, it has been confirmed that Olmo has suffered an adductor tear, which will rule him out of action for four weeks. As such, he will be unavailable to face Real Madrid at the Spotify Camp Nou this Sunday in La Liga. Another blow for Barcelona This comes as the latest in a series of injury concerns for Barcelona leading up to the heavyweight clash against Real Madrid. The current La Liga leaders already lost both Eric Garcia and Jules Kounde to injuries this past weekend during their game against Real Betis. Dani Olmo will miss the Clasico . (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) Their availability for the first Clasico of the season remains uncertain, with now Olmo also joining them on the sidelines. Andreas Christensen, too, is unavailable with an injury, while Roony Bardghji is a long-term absentee. Along with the injuries, the Blaugrana have suffered their first defeat of the season against PSG, leaving them in a vulnerable position ahead of the weekend’s heavyweight clash. This situation could present Real Madrid with a great opportunity to capitalise on and come away with all three points from Catalonia this weekend. As things stand, Jose Mourinho & co. are third in the La Liga standings, six points behind their arch-rivals, and one below second-placed Atletico Madrid.

item.title: Jordan Elliott release, explained: Titans player involved in gun incident at team facility
item.description: Jordan Elliott release, explained: Titans player involved in gun incident at team facility originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Tennessee Titans are coming off their first win of the season, but the team had a serious situation to handle around the game. The Titans released veteran defensive tackle Jordan Elliott on Tuesday unexpectedly after what the team described as "an incident" at its practice facility. Elliott signed a two-year, $8 million deal with the Titans in the offseason, following head coach Robert Saleh to Tennessee from the San Francisco 49ers . Further reporting on the matter revealed that the incident involving Elliott escalated to the point where the defensive tackle went to get a gun from his car during the workday. While the incident ultimately de-escalated, the Titans decided that it was enough to move on from Elliott in the middle of the season. Here's a breakdown of what happened with Jordan Elliott. MORE : Full timeline of Jalen Hurts' blood clot issues, information Jordan Elliott release The Titans announced on Tuesday that they released defensive tackle Jordan Elliott following an incident involving Elliott last week. “On Thursday, October 15, there was an incident at our team facility involving Jordan Elliott," the team said in a statement . "Following our review of the incident, we have made the decision to release Elliott from our roster. We will have no further comment on the matter." Tennessee did not initially reveal any details about the situation, but Elliott was not active on Sunday for the first time this season. Later in the day, Easton Freeze of A to Z Sports said that Elliott's release happened because he got into an altercation with teammate JC Latham on the practice field on Thursday, after which he went to get a gun from his car before John Franklin-Myers talked him down. MORE: 5 ways Sean McVay has failed the Rams so far in 2026 Why did Jordan Elliott retrieve a gun? The Titans didn't describe the incident between Elliott and Latham upon releasing the defensive tackle, but Elliott had reportedly been dealing with issues away from the facility. Then, in practice on Thursday, Elliott and Latham got into a fight, which resulted in the coaching staff telling Elliott to leave the field. After practice, Elliott apparently went to get a gun from his car before John Franklin-Myers talked him down. "Jordan has been having a lot of problems away from the building and obviously he brought it to work with him," a source told reporter Aaron Wilson . "There was no reason for him to go off like that. Everyone thought that was wild. To overreact like that is absolutely crazy. We're just glad that no one got hurt and it's over." item.title: Schottenheimer wants to stop making mistakes, but it's more than that
item.description: The Dallas Cowboys had to go into their boogie man's house and fell short across the board, losing 23-13 to the Green Bay Packers . No part of the team played well in the first half, falling down 17-0, with the offense having two turnovers and the defense allowing a 90% conversion rate on third down. The team was lucky the Packers dropped multiple touchdown passes, keeping the game competitive. Head coach Brian Schottenheimer said the effort was right, but the team needs to eliminate mistakes; the issues seem much deeper than on-field mistakes. The offense didn’t bounce back in the second half. Green Bay offered very little offensively in the third and fourth quarters, but Dallas couldn’t do anything to make the game close . They had their offensive line intact, the three main receivers were healthy, Dak Prescott was under center, Javonte Williams was a full go at running back, and Brevyn Spann-Ford replaced a healthy Jake Ferguson at tight end. With all that at their disposal, Dallas had a single score while the game was in the balance. It was an unacceptable performance from that side of the ball, and putting it all on "mistakes" isn't good enough. Third down is the main issue with the Dallas defense It’s not difficult to figure out the issue with the Dallas defense. They allowed 17 points in the first half and it could’ve been more if not for self-inflicted mistakes by the Packers. The Cowboys allowed four third-down conversions on the opening drive. Two from third-and-13, a third-and-5 and a touchdown on third-and-six. They ended the half allowing 9 of 10 third-down conversions, and for the second time in just six games this season. This allowed GB to run 39 plays to the Cowboys' 23 and control the clock 17 minutes to 13, while the Packers only rushed for 2.7 yards per carry in the opening two quarters. item.title: Today in Motorsport History, October 21: Räikkönen Wins the 2007 Brazilian Grand Prix and the F1 Title by One Point
item.description: Ferrari has not produced a Formula 1 drivers’ champion since Kimi Räikkönen at the 2007 Brazilian Grand Prix. File image from Melbourne. Photo: Ken So / Unsplash Kimi Räikkönen started the last race of 2007 third in the standings, seven points behind a rookie and three behind a two-time champion. By the end of the afternoon he was the Formula 1 world champion. Räikkönen won the 2007 Brazilian Grand Prix at Interlagos on October 21, 2007, 19 years ago today. Lewis Hamilton’s McLaren suffered a gearbox glitch early, and Ferrari ran a one-two that put Räikkönen’s 110 points one clear of both McLaren drivers on 109. It was the first time since 1986 that three drivers had arrived at a season finale with a chance at the title. It is also the last time a Ferrari driver has won it. Seventeen points down with two races to go The 2007 season belonged to McLaren for most of its length, and so did the trouble. Hamilton, in his debut season, and Fernando Alonso, who had just won back-to-back titles with Renault, spent the year taking points off each other in identical cars. Meanwhile, the espionage case involving Ferrari technical data ended with McLaren excluded from the constructors’ championship. Räikkönen, in his first year at Ferrari after replacing Michael Schumacher, looked out of it with two races left. He was 17 points behind Hamilton. However, Hamilton scored nothing in China while Räikkönen won there, his fifth victory of the season. As a result, Hamilton went to Brazil on 107 points, Alonso on 103 and Räikkönen on 100. What each driver needed at the 2007 Brazilian Grand Prix Under the 10-8-6-5-4-3-2-1 points system, Hamilton controlled the title. A fifth-place finish would have been enough whatever his rivals did. Alonso had to recover a four-point gap to his teammate while also keeping Räikkönen behind him. Räikkönen’s path was the narrowest. He needed to win, with Alonso no higher than third and Hamilton no higher than sixth. A sixth place for Hamilton would have tied them on 110, but Räikkönen would have taken the title on wins. In other words, the Finn needed his own perfect day and a bad one for both McLarens. Hamilton (107): fifth or better and the title was his. Alonso (103): needed a strong finish, ideally a win or second place, and help from Hamilton’s result. Räikkönen (100): win, Alonso third or lower, Hamilton sixth or lower. Lap one and a gearbox glitch Felipe Massa took pole at his home race, and Hamilton started alongside him. Räikkönen started third and Alonso fourth. At the start, Massa squeezed Hamilton, Räikkönen went around the outside into second, and Alonso passed Hamilton for third. Then Hamilton tried to retake the place down the hill into Turn 4, locked up, ran wide and rejoined eighth. Eighth was still recoverable. What came next was not. A few laps later Hamilton’s McLaren slowed sharply with an electronic gearbox problem, and by the time the car came back to life he had dropped to 18th. He spent the rest of the afternoon climbing back through the field on a three-stop strategy, but he could not get higher than seventh. Fans on the terraces at Interlagos, where three drivers arrived with a shot at the 2007 title. File image from the 2022 race weekend. Photo: Eduardo Taulois / Unsplash How Ferrari swapped its leaders in the pits With Hamilton out of the picture, the title came down to the order of the two Ferraris. Massa led, Räikkönen sat behind him, and Alonso ran a distant third. If the race finished that way, Hamilton would keep the crown. Ferrari settled it with fuel and timing rather than team orders on track. Both cars made their first stops on lap 21. For the second round, Massa pitted from the lead on lap 50. Räikkönen stayed out until lap 53 and used the light-fuel laps to build enough time to rejoin ahead. When the stops shook out, Räikkönen led Massa, and the championship order flipped. Räikkönen won by 1.493 seconds. Massa finished second, and Alonso was third, 57 seconds back. Hamilton crossed the line seventh. Pit-stop timing decided the lead at Interlagos in 2007, when Räikkönen stayed out three laps longer than Massa. File image from 2022. Photo: Eduardo Taulois / Unsplash One point, and a protest that changed nothing The final table read Räikkönen 110, Hamilton 109, Alonso 109. Hamilton took second on countback. Räikkönen, who had finished second at Interlagos in each of the previous three years, became Finland’s third world champion after Keke Rosberg and Mika Häkkinen. Afterward he credited a team that, in his words, “always believed we could recover.” Ferrari also took the constructors’ title. There was one more twist. After the race, the FIA technical delegate reported that fuel in the BMW Sauber and Williams cars was more than 10°C below ambient temperature, which the rules did not allow. The stewards declined to penalize them, citing doubt over the true fuel and ambient temperatures. McLaren appealed. Had those cars been excluded, Hamilton would have moved up to fourth and won the title. In November 2007, the FIA International Court of Appeal ruled McLaren’s appeal inadmissible, and the result stood. Why the 2007 Brazilian Grand Prix still matters It is still Ferrari’s last drivers’ title. Massa came within one point at the same circuit a year later. Since then, Ferrari has won races and the 2008 constructors’ championship, but no Ferrari driver has been crowned. Every season that passes makes October 21, 2007, a bigger date in Maranello’s history. Ferrari’s modern title era began with Schumacher ending a 21-year wait at Suzuka in 2000 , and Räikkönen’s title remains its last entry. It shaped Hamilton’s career. The rookie lost the title by one point at Interlagos. Twelve months later, he won it there by one point over Massa, passing Timo Glock on the final lap to take the fifth place he needed. That pairing of results is one reason the circuit carries so much weight in his story. It closed an era of driver aids. Brazil 2007 was the last Grand Prix before the FIA’s standard ECU, supplied by McLaren Electronic Systems, arrived for 2008. The change banned traction control and electronic engine-braking aids, and that put car control back in drivers’ hands. It belongs to a long line of one-point finishes. The 2007 decider sits alongside Mike Hawthorn’s one-point title in 1958 as proof that a championship can turn on a single position. Fittingly, Räikkönen’s 21st and final Grand Prix win came on October 21, 2018, in Austin, 11 years to the day after Interlagos. He retired after the 2021 season with that single world title. Nineteen years on, the lesson from Interlagos still applies to the current fight. As Kimi Antonelli heads to Austin with a chance to seal the 2026 title, the records he could break are a reminder that a lead is never final until the math says so. The nearly $150 million demand stands out because of the amount involved in a lawsuit between two racing teams. JGR initially sought more than $8 million in damages when it filed the case. The much larger figure now puts the financial stakes on a different scale, with the latest reporting describing the claim as unusually large for a team-versus-team dispute. Although lawsuits involving NASCAR ’s wider corporate structure have involved substantial financial stakes, this case is different: JGR is pursuing another team and a former executive over alleged trade secret misappropriation. item.title: Third time this century - how Australia's stark collapse unfolded
item.description: 99 is Australia's lowest score in Tests since being bowled out for 91 by India in Nagpur in 2023 [Getty Images] Second Test, Gqeberha (day four of five) South Africa 425-9 dec: Bavuma 179, Jansen 85; Boland 5-81 Australia 99: Smith 28; Jansen 5-33 Australia trail by 422 runs Scorecard Australia were forced to follow-on for only the third time in the past 38 years after being dismissed for 99 by South Africa on day four of the second Test in Gqeberha. Left-armer Marco Jansen took a superb 5-33 and Kagiso Rabada and Wiaan Mulder two wickets each as the Proteas roared back into the Test to give them a real shot at leveling the series. They were 110-6 early on day three, their hopes severely dented, but scrapped to 425-9 after Temba Bavuma's 179 and now take a 326-run first innings lead. Australia's surrender was stark. After opener Nic Maddinson was dismissed late on day three, South Africa took the remaining nine wickets inside 40 overs on the fourth day. Steve Smith was the tourists highest scoring with 28. No other batter passed 14 and the highest partnership was just 23. The last time Australia were forced to follow-on was against India at Sydney in 2019. Before that, the most recent previous occasion was the fourth Ashes Test at Trent Bridge in 2005. It was also the biggest first-innings deficit they conceded since a Test against West Indies in November 1984. How Australia's collapse unfolded Jansen sparked the collapse by nicking off nightwatchman Scott Boland with his first ball of the day at the start of the second over. Four overs later he pinned Travis Head lbw on review for 14 and Marnus Labuschagne was brilliantly caught at slip by Simon Harmer off the bowling of Anrich Nortje for the same score. Nortje was only able to bowl 3.3 overs because of an apparent groin issue, which will impact the remainder of the Test if he is unable to bowl again. After Jansen found the edge of Matt Renshaw and Alex Carey in the same over, he also had Beau Webster caught in similar fashion for his fifth Test five-wicket haul. Mitchell Starc and Australia captain Pat Cummins followed within 11 balls of Mulder bowling Smith, who had been given treatment to his neck throughout his 88 balls, and, after a brief conversation with his bowlers, captain Bavuma signaled to Australia's dressing room that they would have to bat again. South Africa now have more than 150 overs to complete victory. Notifications, social media and more with BBC Sport

item.title: Problem or Solution: Jarren Duran
item.description: The Boston Red Sox are stuck. If you’re the type of person who is content finishing third within the division and being bounced by your arch rivals in just a handful of games in back-to-back seasons, you might disagree. If you’re not an idiot, you know difficult decisions need to be made and that things need to change. I’ve decided to task myself with analyzing which players can be part of the turnaround and which should be shown the door, all as a way to take the heat off chief baseball officer Craig Breslow. If you’re not down with that, I’ve got two words for ya: Problem or Solution? Jarren Duran It’s time to rip the band-aid off and talk about the most polarizing player in the organization… Jarren Duran has not-so-slowly devolved from being the heart and soul of the team to dead weight, doing it within three seasons. I’ll go ahead and lay out the numbers for you below, which illustrate just part of the reason we’re even having this conversation… 2024: .285/.342/.492, 21 HR, 75 RBI, 48 2B, 14 3B, 34 SB, 132 OPS+ 2025: .256/.332/.442, 16 HR, 84 RBI, 41 2B, 13 3B, 24 SB, 114 OPS+ 2026: .208/.207/.361, 20 HR, 69 RBI, 15 2B, 5 3B, 21 SB, 76 OPS+ … with the other reason(s) being his penchant for getting into trouble by flipping off fans, using homophobic slurs, threatening to beat up podcasters, and all sorts of other stuff. I’d like to stick to on-field factors, but it’s kind of impossible with this guy in particular. JARREN DURAN JUST STOLE HOME!!!! pic.twitter.com/fcLZx7cgk9 — Red Sox (@RedSox) April 26, 2025 WHAT WE KNOW Duran has worn out his welcome, with all of the things we previously laid out seemingly working together to limit his effectiveness on the field. Duran still showcased an ability to hit for power and cause havoc on the base paths last season, but the consistency was gone and much of that had to do with the fact that he wasn’t entrusted with a full-time role until Roman Anthony was injured on May 4. I’d imagine they aren’t going to suddenly trust him more after the season he just had season, especially with the organization expected to lean on that trio of Anthony, Ceddanne Rafaela, and Wilyer Abreu. WHAT WE DON’T KNOW If any of those three players get hurt, which history tells us is just a matter of time, there will be tons of questions surrounding the overall depth of the outfield. Nate Eaton, Jahmai Jones, and Mickey Gasper were getting significant at-bats down the stretch, dude. I don’t have to tell you how bad that is, so while it hurts me to admit, there is at least a track record to look back at with Duran. Page points to the Muhammad Ali Act - a 2000 US law designed to protect boxers' rights and combat potential monopolies - as something which he'd like to replicate in MMA. "It's less about speaking out now, it's more about forming a union and coming together. We have to move as one," Page told BBC Sport. "If all fighters said 'we're not gonna do it', then UFC doesn't exist. That's the important thing for fighters to remember. item.title: Jury selection set for trial of driver in Gaudreau crash
item.description: Jury selection is to begin Dec. 1 for the motorist who fatally struck hockey star Johnny Gaudreau and his brother as they bicycled on a rural road in South Jersey in August 2024. Superior Court Judge Michael Silvanio has set the process to begin at 9 a.m. in his courtroom at the Salem County Courthouse. Trial is scheduled to begin Jan. 4 for the driver, 45-year-old Sean Higgins of Pilesgrove. Court fight: Judge in Gaudreau brothers' case won't dismiss indictment Authorities say Higgins struck Johnny Gaudreau, 31, and Matty Gaudreau, 29, as the brothers bicycled on Aug. 29 at approximately 8:20 p.m. on a narrow road in Salem County. Separately, previously unreleased photographs from the accident scene have been made public as part of an Oct. 5 filing by Higgins' defense attorneys. The photos include images of two bicycles shattered by the accident and of Higgins' damaged Jeep. Among other points, the defense filing disputes the prosecution's account of how the accident occurred. It describes as "impossible" the prosecution's assertion that Higgins was passing a vehicle on the right, with his Jeep half on the road's shoulder and half on grass, when he struck the brothers at high speed. Higgins' attorneys — Richard Klineburger III and Matthew Portello, both of Haddonfield — also dispute the prosecution's claim that the driver was drunk at the time of the accident. The Gaudreaus, both of whom were expectant fathers, died at the scene. Johnny Gaudreau was an all-star for the NHL's Columbus Blue Jackets. Known as "Johnny Hockey," he and his brother were South Jersey natives and graduates of Gloucester Catholic High School in Gloucester City. An indictment accuses Higgins of two counts of reckless vehicular homicide while driving drunk. He also faces charges of aggravated manslaughter, evidence tampering and leaving the scene of a fatal accident. The charges are only allegations. Higgins has not been convicted in the case. He has been held in Salem County Jail since the crash. Jim Walsh is a senior reporter with the Courier-Post, Burlington County Times and The Daily Journal. Email: Jwalsh@cpsj.com. item.title: Sturgis 200 medley relay team clocks state-qualifying time
item.description: The Sturgis swim team has continued to improve in the pool this season. The Trojans are not a big team by numbers, but solid performances throughout the season have helped them continue to gain confidence. The Trojans traveled north to take on Mason, Otsego and Wayland in prep swimming action last Saturday, Oct. 17. The highlight for the Trojans was the 200 medley relay team, which qualified for the state finals this year in a time of 1:58.09. The team of Brooklyn Draper, Lilly Whitehead, Ainsley Gump and Katelyn Halling brought home first place in that race. For the meet, Sturgis racked up 554 points in the pool, beating Mason's 524, Wayland's 498 and Otsego's 196. Gump swam to first place in the 200 freestyle at 2:02.21 and was first in the 100 freestyle race at 55.96 seconds. REST OF THE WEEK: Here's a look at the prep sports schedule for the week October 19-24 WEEK 9 FOTBALL PRIMER: Week 9 football primer | Sturgis, Three Rivers renew rivalry in finale The Lady Trojans have now claimed victory in four meets this season, including three in the conference to date. Sturgis also claimed first place in the 200 freestyle relay. There, the team of Gump, Ella Whitehead, Lilly Whitehead and Halling posted 1:47.01 to win. The Trojans were upended 119-63 last week against the Harper Creek Beavers. Herblet won the 200 freestyle at 2:15.53, and Gump won the 200 individual medley at 2:19.77. Gump also swam to first place in the 100 fly with a time of 1:06.97. The Trojans got a victory from the 200 freestyle relay as well with Gump, Whitehead, Whitehead and Halling recording a time of 1:49.05 to pace the field. Sturgis did beat rival Marshall in the pool recently as well, 93-72. That matchup saw Gump finish with a time of 2:13.63, which set a new pool record at Marshall. She won the race. Gump also took first place in the 100 fly on the day with a time of 1:12.73. The 200 medley team picked up a victory in Marshall at 2:01.00 with Gump, Draper, Lilly Whitehead and Halling. They set a MISCA cut time with that race. Also registering wins in Marshall were Herblet in the 200 freestyle at 2:19.49; Halling in the sprint freestyles (27.44 seconds in the 50 and 1:03.42 in the 100); Draper in the 100 backstroke (1:11.22) and the 200 freestyle relay team of Whitehead, Whitehead, Halling and Gump at 1:50.03. item.title: Hoffenheim vs. Lyon preview: Team news & predicted lineups
item.description: Hoffenheim vs. Lyon preview: Team news & predicted lineups After a much-needed 2-1 win over fellow Bundesliga strugglers Borussia Mönchengladbach ended their four-game losing streak at the weekend, TSG Hoffenheim will be looking to build on that result when they face Olympique Lyon in the Europa League on Thursday. Die Kraichgauer desperately need points in the Europa League, having lost 2-0 to both OFI and Besiktas in their first two games in the competition this season. By contrast, Lyon have won both of their Europa League encounters so far, beating Anderlecht 2-1 away from home before edging Crystal Palace 3-2 on home soil. Paulo Fonseca's side have also impressed domestically, maintaining top spot on goal difference ahead of Paris Saint-Germain with a 2-1 win over OGC Nice at the weekend. The two teams also met in the Europa League in 2024, playing out a 2-2 draw in a game that saw Umut Tohumcu rescue a point for Hoffenheim with a late equaliser in injury time. Team news and predicted lineups: TSG Hoffenheim will have to manage without Nathan de Cat, Albian Hajdari and Patrick Wimmer, who are all injured. Head coach Christian Ilzer could rotate his side, as he has done in Europe earlier this season, with Kicker speculating that Valentin Gendrey could be handed his first start of the campaign at right-back at the expense of veteran Vladimir Coufal. Further forward, veteran striker Andrej Kramarić is among those likely to come into the starting lineup, having played a more marginal role this season and been limited to just 12 minutes against Gladbach at the weekend. As for Lyon, Paulo Fonseca is also likely to make some changes to his side, having similarly rotated his squad in Europe this season. Loïs Openda, Mohamadi Ouedraogo and Nicolás Tagliafico are set to miss out through injury for the visitors. Click here to see our predicted Hoffenheim vs. Lyon lineups.

item.title: Essex sign wicketkeeper Bell from Lancashire
item.description: George Bell spent the end of the 2026 season on loan at Essex [Getty Images] Essex have signed wicketkeeper George Bell from Lancashire on a permanent two-year deal after a productive loan spell last season. The 24-year-old made three Essex appearances at the end of the 2026 campaign, scoring a half-century in each innings and finishing in the 60s on every occasion. "I believe this is an environment that will help me to develop my game further and hopefully contribute to Essex wins and trophies," Bell told the club's website. Bell made his first-class debut for Lancashire in 2022, and has represented England at under-21 level. Across 37 first-class matches, he has scored more than 1,400 runs, including nine half-centuries, with a high score of 99. Essex's director of cricket, Chris Silverwood, said: "Not only were George's performances impressive on the field, but the way he carried himself, his attitude, work ethic and mindset also impressed us. "We felt George had more than earned the opportunity to join us on a permanent deal, and we are delighted to now have him. He has already shown what he can bring to the team, and we are all excited about his addition to the squad."

item.title: Newcastle wants to beat Juventus to English defender
item.description: Newcastle wants to beat Juventus to English defender Juventus were keen to sign Fikayo Tomori during the summer before deciding to pursue Jhon Lucumi instead. However, the Bianconeri remain interested in the AC Milan defender, particularly with his contract situation potentially allowing them to sign him as a free agent. Tomori remains an experienced centre back who has established himself in Serie A. His quality and familiarity with Italian football make him an attractive option for Juventus as they consider ways to strengthen their defence. However, Juventus are not the only club monitoring his situation. With the possibility of signing him without paying a transfer fee, several teams could compete for his signature, making the race more difficult for the Italian giants. Newcastle enter the race for Tomori According to Football Insider , Newcastle United are the latest club to show interest in signing Tomori. The Premier League side reportedly views the defender as one of their leading transfer targets for the summer and would be keen to persuade him to return to England. A move back to the Premier League could appeal to Tomori, who would have the opportunity to continue his career in familiar surroundings. Newcastle could also offer a competitive financial package if he becomes available as a free agent. Juventus would therefore need to make an attractive proposal to remain in contention. Although they have tracked the defender for some time, their interest alone will not guarantee that he chooses to continue playing in Italy. (Photo by Marco Rosi – SS Lazio/Getty Images) Juventus face competition for his signature The prospect of signing Tomori without a transfer fee makes him an appealing target for both clubs. Juventus could strengthen their defensive options without paying Milan a transfer fee, but they may have to compete financially with Newcastle to secure an agreement. The Bianconeri remain capable of winning the race, provided they can offer terms that satisfy the defender. However, Newcastle’s interest could complicate their plans, particularly if the English club makes a serious effort to bring him home. Newcastle’s own season has been turbulent, and their final league position remains uncertain. That could influence their transfer plans and their ability to attract targets. For Juventus, Tomori remains a potential opportunity, but the club must be prepared for competition. If Newcastle pursue him aggressively, the financial terms and sporting project offered by both sides could prove decisive in determining his next destination.

item.title: Roma’s Champions League earnings reach €52 million
item.description: Roma’s Champions League earnings reach €52 million Roma are back on track in the Champions League, and financially, too. After losing to José Mourinho’s Real Madrid, Gian Piero Gasperini’s side swept Slovan Bratislava 4-0, securing their first win of the League Phase. This result allows the Giallorossi to climb to four points in the standings, following their opening draw against Fenerbahçe. More importantly, their European success guarantees the club an immediate bonus of €2.1 million, in addition to the €700,000 already earned on Matchday 1. Participation in Europe’s premier competition represents a particularly significant source of revenue for the Roman club. According to Calcio e Finanza estimates, Roma has already reached €52.19 million in total revenue from the 2026-2027 Champions League. This sum is made up of several components, starting with the €18.62 million guaranteed simply by qualifying for the league phase. Added to these are the 2.8 million earned through on-field results and a minimum share of 275 thousand euros tied to the final placing.

item.title: Real Betis midfielder Facundo Bernal slapped with heavy ban after 'headbutt' assault on Barcelona star Lamine Yamal
item.description: Real Betis Balompie v FC Barcelona - LaLiga EA Sports 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Real Betis midfielder Facundo Bernal has been slapped with a four-game suspension following a fiery clash with Barcelona forward Lamine Yamal. The Uruguayan was sent off after headbutting the teenager during a dramatic 5-2 defeat at the weekend. Big suspension confirmed Bernal has been given a four-game ban by the Royal Spanish Football Federation (RFEF) disciplinary committee on Wednesday. The sanction comes following his sending off during a 5-2 defeat against Barca at the weekend. Bernal was sent off in the 54th minute, shortly after Betis scored to narrow the deficit to 3-2. His dismissal completely swung the momentum of the high-stakes match back in favor of the opposition. The 23-year-old midfielder will now face an extended period on the sidelines. His actions have drawn severe disciplinary consequences from the Spanish governing body. Clash with Lamine Yamal The disciplinary report published on Wednesday by the RFEF outlined the specific reasons behind the harsh punishment. According to the official report, Bernal grabbed Yamal by the neck before headbutting him twice. The Uruguayan international was deemed to have assaulted Yamal while the ball was not in play. The governing body's disciplinary code strictly dictates that bans range from four to 12 games for such violent behaviour. Bernal ultimately received the minimum penalty permitted under the regulations for the offense. Yamal was also booked during the heated exchange for pushing the Betis midfielder prior to the red-card incident. Real Betis Balompie v FC Barcelona - LaLiga EA Sports 2026/27 More disciplinary trouble The match unravelled completely for Betis following the red card. Barca capitalised on the numerical advantage to score three unanswered goals, with Yamal assisting Gabriel Jesus for the third effort. The fallout extended beyond the pitch as well. Betis sporting director Manu Fajardo was also sanctioned with a two-game suspension and a fine for conduct contrary to good sporting order. Key matches missed Bernal will miss a crucial run of Liga fixtures for Betis. He is set to sit out upcoming matches against Celta Vigo, Malaga, Elche, and the fierce derby clash with Sevilla on November 22. The suspension serves as a significant blow to the squad's midfield depth during a crucial phase of the campaign. Betis currently sit fourth in the Liga standings on 19 points.

item.title: Van Dijk says 'risk' is worth reward under Liverpool boss Iraola
item.description: Villarreal's Nathan-Dylan Saliba (R) and Liverpool's Virgil van Dijk battle for the ball during the UEFA Champions League soccer match between Liverpool FC and Villarreal CF at Anfield. (is associated with: «Van Dijk says 'risk' is worth reward under Liverpool boss Iraola») Nick Potts/PA Wire/dpa Liverpool captain Virgil van Dijk believes the risks associated with playing Andoni Iraola's way is worth the reward - although it helps when you have a teenage winger as exciting as Rio Ngumoha. Villarreal exposed the spaces and flaws in a team showing six changes to take a 2-0 lead inside 30 minutes at Anfield on Tuesday but, inspired by their 18-year-old phenomenon, the hosts fought back to win 4-3 to maintain their 100% Champions League record. The change involved Iraola doubling-down on his high-intensity pressing in the second half, gambling on a man-to-man approach to first nullify the visitors' superior mobility and then turn the game in their favour. Ngumoha's pace and directness was a key factor but the positivity of bringing on Florian Wirtz at half-time and dropping previous number 10 Ryan Gravenberch to right-back was rewarded with a third successive win. It was the first time Liverpool had come from 2-0 down to win in the Champions League since beating Villarreal in the 2022 semi-final. "Obviously we don't want to put ourselves in a position where you have to come back from anything and that's what I did from the start," said Van Dijk, who was at pains to take responsibility for "a bad day at the office" after his individual error led to conceding the first goal. "It wasn't a great first half but we got it turned around. When it pays off, yes definitely (it's exciting). "But when you just mistime the tackle or when they flick it then it could be wide open but that was definitely the message: we have to go all-in if we try to win the ball up high and you have to take that risk and second half we were much better." Ngumoha was deservedly awarded man of the match as, in addition to his two assists for Alexis Mac Allister, he was, in Van Dijk's words, "pretty electric". The 18-year-old has completed more successful dribbles (16) than any player in the Champions League, with Barcelona's Ballon d'Or contender Lamine Yamal four behind in second place. "He was a complete threat constantly and their defender had a tough time," added Van Dijk, who believes spending last season in the same squad as Mohamed Salah was of huge benefit. "Everyone is chipping in but for him to work with Mo last year was obviously massive as Mo was one of the best wingers at the club and experienced everything, so why not soak in all the information and show it on the pitch and show your own qualities? "I think he has shown it this season but there is still much more to come."

item.title: What are the EFL rules on homegrown players?
item.description: Watford are among the clubs who have a number of homegrown players that do not represent England or Wales [Getty Images] In the Championship, League One and League Two, clubs must have a minimum of eight homegrown players registered in their squad. For a league game in the EFL, clubs must name at least seven homegrown players in their matchday squad. A homegrown player is someone who has been registered with either their current club, or any English or Welsh club, for a period of three seasons or 36 months prior to either their 21st birthday, or the end of the season that the player in question turns 21. These rules are only enforced in league matches and are not enforced by the EFL for the FA Cup, EFL Cup or EFL Trophy. The Premier League operates its own separate system of rules on squad lists and homegrown players. An example of the rule classifying players as homegrown, despite not being English or Welsh, can be seen in Watford's recent 2-0 win over Charlton Athletic. Watford defenders Mattie Pollock and Marc Bola were the only players who are listed as English in the Hornets matchday squad. However, Hector Kyprianou (Cyprus), Jordan Zemura (Zimbabwe), Daniel Bachmann (Austria), Stephy Mavididi (Democratic Republic of Congo) and Amin Nabizada (Afghanistan), who all represent other countries for international games, are classed as homegrown due to where they played their club football as youth players. Once an EFL club has submitted its squad list following the conclusion of the summer transfer window, each club is required to list at least one club-developed player per match on its squad list or team sheet. For any match in which a club fails to do so, they are permitted one fewer player on their bench for the game. In the Championship, that would mean eight substitutes instead of nine, and in League One and League Two, it would result in six substitutes instead of seven. Players aged under 21 do not count towards squad lists across all three EFL leagues, while goalkeepers are not included in the squad lists for League One and League Two. There’s a difference between surrendering a fifth-rounder for a veteran who can contribute immediately and giving away premium draft capital because the team unexpectedly won four games. item.title: Too much Overlap? Gary Neville’s podcast empire knows no bounds
item.description: The Overlap has gone daily, with Steven Gerrard and Joe Hart among the latest additions to an ever-growing family Viewed in 2026, Nathan Barley, Chris Morris’s 2005 sitcom, shows remarkable prescience about the last two decades of metropolitan life, from smartphone addiction and digital derangement to sheer existential vapidity. When Barley’s character referred to his occupation as “self-facilitating media node”, Morris and co-writer Charlie Brooker were way ahead on the creator economy. What the pair failed to predict was ex-footballers joining the sector in droves. These days, if you are a former footballer without a podcast or YouTube channel, then did you ever really play the game? Setting aside the Gary Lineker Goalhanger empire, manspreading its centrist-dad agenda into issues way beyond guffaws with Micah Richards and Alan Shearer, there is Gary Neville to rule them all. Manchesterism’s second-most influential practitioner has been on heavy manoeuvres. Unlike Lineker’s productions, the Overlap’s output continues to stick largely to football; a rugby podcast was mothballed in February, though its cricket equivalent continues. Continue reading...

Those in attendance, officially 40,042 but that felt optimistic, saw Foden shine on the right wing and as a central striker, showing there is life without Erling Haaland, who watched from the bench. Admittedly, the opposition were not a match for the Premier League side, whose other goals came from Elliot Anderson and Rayan Cherki. Stavros Pilios’s consolation was more a reward for the boisterous fans in yellow and black, who created the atmosphere, than for the overall efforts of the visitors. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Kulusevski and Maddison return to form but are Tottenham also back?
item.description: As Tottenham edged to victory over Coventry , a familiar face among the post-match salutations. Could that be Dejan Kulusevski? For it was he, playing 526 days since his last Spurs appearance. Much has changed though still much stays the same. Ben Davies’s deflected late clincher catapulted Spurs up to … 16th. When Kulusevski last played on 11 May 2025, Tottenham were 17th, the position in which they finished both that season and in 2025-26. Further to Peters and Lee [ Monday’s Football Daily letters] another 70s example that occurred to me was the West Ham players Mervyn Day and Bill Green . They were both in the West Ham United team from 1976-78, and in Carlisle United’s greatest season 1974-75. When Green was still at Carlisle, he played against West Ham’s Day. So plenty of Green Day commentary opportunities there. Of course, the band hadn’t formed yet, but who knows, perhaps they thought of the band’s name whilst watching some old 70s football footage” – Bob Dunning. On the subject of musical football matchups, all I can say is that it’s just a shame Gareth Barry was at Manchester City a few years too late to play alongside David White ” – Tim Russell. As an aside to the music makers and fitba’, in the late 60s at the old Highbury, we would be entertained at every first team match by the local constabulary brass band. Such was the style of play, it did introduce a some element of entertainment into our visits to the old stadium” – Tommy Boyd (and, surprisingly, others). His work here was done, Hansi Flick invited him to take the weight off his feet and his shoulders, not that he wanted to. First, though, he took Lamine Yamal’s head in his hands and, leaning in away from the amateur lip readers, tried to make himself heard over the noise. “I told him I was proud of him because he played a fantastic game,” he said. At least he could think of something. When Lamine Yamal had opened the scoring just nine minutes into the match that was supposed to find out how good Barcelona really were, it hadn’t been easy. Nothing erudite, anyway. Valdano had just watched Lamine do that , whatever that was , in Istanbul – an “almost rabona ”, the kid called it – and now he had a problem. “If he keeps doing strange things, we’re not going to be able to explain it,” he wrote . item.title: Brighton are the apex B club – their next target should be a Champions League place | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. item.title: ‘Leaving England is scary but I’m here to win’: Charlie Cresswell on Ligue 1 life and his international dream
item.description: Young centre-back could not see a way forward at Leeds so moved to France. Now he’s preparing for the biggest game of his life against Juventus By Get French Football News “Leaving England is such a scary, scary decision,” says Charlie Cresswell. item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.description: A match delayed by missile attack warnings is not what Cristiano Ronaldo and co signed up for but it’s the new reality; the Saudi sporting juggernaut is stalling Cristiano Ronaldo grabbed the scarf in the colours of the Saudi Arabian flag and waved it at the sparse but enthusiastic crowd, who responded with rapturous cheers. It was a gesture of defiance rather than a victory salute, encapsulating the Saudi equivalent of “Keep calm and carry on”. Monday night’s Asian Champions League Elite game between Al-Nassr and the Uzbek side Neftchi Fergana had ended with a 3-1 win for the Saudi club coached by Ange Postecoglou, with Ronaldo, supported by Sadio Mané, scoring, the smattering of star names indicative of the lure of the Saudi Pro League. Yet this isn’t quite how Ronaldo and co would have anticipated life in Riyadh. The meagre attendance aside, Monday’s game was delayed by a threat of missile attacks from Yemen’s Houthi rebels. A safety warning issued 15 minutes before kick-off came two days after 13 people died and more than 300 were wounded by Houthi strikes on Riyadh’s King Khalid international airport. item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! There are only two things certain in life – death and taxes Reece James knack and Watford managerial news – and Football Daily’s bingo card lit up with both on Friday. But while Chelsea’s statement on their crocked right-back having successful knee surgery was a cut-and-paste job from the last time James was injured, the quotes by Watford manager Alessio Dionisi were much more exciting, mainly because it contained an actual apology to Elton John and the remarkable news that the club’s trigger-happy owners have not already sent the Italian the same way as an apple in Michael Owen’s house . item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! It is quite funny that PSG felt like the good guys at the Etihad Stadium but if we briefly detach ourselves from the notion that the European champions’ own sportswashing and cashsplashing has also done immeasurable damage to the beautiful game, then their 4-2 Bigger Cup shellacking of Manchester City was pure cinema, baby! I was stunned at reading the comments in support of Manchester City keeping their trophies, coming out of the mouth of their Bigger Cup rivals at PSG (yesterday’s Quote of the Day). Given the example of the organisers of the Tour de Lance … sorry, the Tour de France, this kind of ‘keep the awards you won’ stuff might get him sent to the Bastille. Or consider Formula One. They’ve got all kinds of rules about driver behaviour on the racetrack, and additional rules about what the crew can and cannot do to your car. Cars get inspected before each race, and there are also mandatory post-race inspections for every car. You might drive your car first across the line to the cheers of the crowd, but if the post-race inspection discovered that you cheated in how your team designed your vehicle, your memory of crossing the line is all you get to keep. Think about that for a minute. If the Premier League and Fifa cannot clear the bar for morals in sport set by the UCI and FIA, that says a lot. And none of it good” – Peter Rehwaldt. My friend Bernard grew up in Coventry. And as a boy he thought the team was called ‘Coventry City Nil’. I would get out more, but I’m a Manchester United fan” – Brendan Hughes. item.title: Robbie Savage the panto villain puts scepticism aside to leave Leicester reeling
item.description: Peterborough’s new boss has long been a divisive figure but a stunning 3-1 win at struggling former club offered a glimpse of his fearless philosophy It felt as though the stars had aligned when Robbie Savage’s first League One match in charge of Peterborough – his first EFL managerial role – happened to be at Leicester. He made his name here and forged a divisive and enduring reputation that has made him a permanent fixture in English football. Savage has long been a joker figure – an image born in his playing days, when he hurtled around midfield with long blond hair bouncing, launching into challenges that at one point made him the most booked player in Premier League history. A pantomime villain, a prankster and an eccentric who was once fined £10,000 by the Football Association – and two weeks’ wages by Leicester – for using the referee Graham Poll’s toilet before a match. (Savage blamed an upset stomach brought on by antibiotics). Continue reading...

item.title: The Premier League so far: draws, underperforming xG and other data pointers
item.description: Goal averages are crumbling as players take fewer touches in the box and forwards underperform against xG Goals are on the up in the Premier League. The average of 2.70 non-penalty goals per game in 2026-27 is higher than last season and two of the four previous campaigns. Yet we should have been even more royally entertained. Matches have averaged 2.88 non-penalty expected goals, the second most in the past six seasons. Chances have been going to waste. If the 20 teams converted at the par rate, there would have been almost two extra goals per week. As few as that sounds, the proportion of games drawn is higher than in any past Premier League season. Some tied matches might have been settled had the finishing been up to the mark. item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17.
